# Standard Cup Reference: Active Compounds in a 250 mL Infusion

This reference consolidates quantitative yields of key active compounds in a standard 250 mL cup of brewed tea, covering green and black tea under typical laboratory extraction and standardized consumer brewing protocols. Values represent typical ranges observed in peer-reviewed literature (Standard Cup Reference pack).

## Factual active compound yield matrix (250 mL infusion)

| Compound | Tea Type | Typical Yield Range | Brewing Conditions | Primary Citation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Caffeine | Green Tea | 30 mg – 50 mg | Loose-leaf green tea; 2 g dry weight; infused in 250 mL water at 80 °C for 3 minutes. | Chin, J. M., et al. (2008). *Journal of Analytical Toxicology, 32*(8), 702-704. |
| Caffeine | Black Tea | 40 mg – 80 mg | Loose-leaf black tea; 2 g dry weight; infused in 250 mL water at 100 °C for 3–5 minutes. | Hicks, M. B., et al. (1996). *Food Chemistry, 56*(4), 425-428. |
| L-Theanine | Green Tea | 15 mg – 30 mg (Note: Shaded Gyokuro or Matcha yields 45–80 mg) | Premium green tea; 2 g dry weight; infused in 250 mL water at 80 °C for 3 minutes. | Keenan, E. K., et al. (2011). *Food Chemistry, 125*(2), 588-594. |
| L-Theanine | Black Tea | 10 mg – 25 mg | Standard black tea blend; 2 g dry weight; infused in 250 mL water at 100 °C for 3–5 minutes. | Keenan, E. K., et al. (2011). *Food Chemistry, 125*(2), 588-594. |
| EGCG | Green Tea | 50 mg – 120 mg | High-grade green tea; 2 g dry weight; infused in 250 mL water at 80 °C for 3 minutes. | Perva-Uzunalic, A., et al. (2006). *Food Chemistry, 96*(4), 597-605. |
| EGCG | Black Tea | 1.0 mg – 10 mg (Note: Converted into TFs or TRs during oxidation) | Standard black tea; 2 g dry weight; infused in 250 mL water at 100 °C for 3–5 minutes. | Del Rio, D., et al. (2004). *Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry, 52*(10), 2807-2815. |
| Total Catechins | Green Tea | 100 mg – 300 mg | Loose-leaf green tea; 2 g dry weight; infused in 250 mL water at 80 °C for 3 minutes. | Bhagwat, S., et al. (2011). USDA Database for the Flavonoid Content of Selected Foods, Release 3.0. |
| Total Catechins | Black Tea | 10 mg – 50 mg (Note: Highly polymerized into theaflavins and thearubigins) | Loose-leaf black tea; 2 g dry weight; infused in 250 mL water at 100 °C for 5 minutes. | Lakenbrink, C., et al. (2000). *Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry, 48*(7), 2575-2582. |

## Critical parameters and variance guidelines

### Water temperature sensitivity

Catechins (especially EGCG) require high activation energy for extraction. Steeping green tea at 100 °C instead of 80 °C increases the total catechin yield by approximately 25 percent, but concurrently increases the extraction of bitter, polymeric proanthocyanidins, ruining the sensory profile.

### Mug size standard

In international scientific literature, a standard cup of tea is evaluated at either 200 mL or 250 mL. To maintain precision across calculators and interfaces on this portal, the typical serving size is fixed at exactly **250 mL (0.25 Liters)**.

### Leaf-to-water ratio

The standardized laboratory and professional tasting protocol (governed by ISO 3103 standards) utilizes 2 g of loose-leaf tea per 100 mL of water (approximately 5 g per 250 mL). The consumer brewing conditions modeled in the reference table above reflect a standard single-teabag or single-teaspoon equivalent of **2 g dry weight per 250 mL cup**, representing the most common dietary baseline.

Document metadata from the Standard Cup Reference pack: target volume 250 mL; standard ISO 3103 (adapted for consumer baseline); status peer-reviewed / active.
